label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
Sizwe, boet. Breathe. Put the phone down on the bonnet, take one big breath — then pick it up again, because this bit matters.

**Key out the ignition.** Not off. Out. Every time that starter turns over, the pump is running on petrol, and petrol doesn't lubricate anything. Leave it alone now.

**Don't put diesel on top.** Kobus means well, he really does, but that's old Land Rover advice — that trick worked on a 1985 diesel, not a 2019 common rail. Pouring diesel into 45 litres of petrol just makes expensive petrol. Mixing does nothing except make the drain job heavier.

And you're not driving it. It was running when it died and you cranked it five or six times after that, so there might be damage to the pump and injectors. That's not me being doom, that's me being straight with you. It gets towed, and somebody inspects it before anything turns again.

**Phone your insurance tonight.** Most policies include a roadside tow. Don't hand a tow guy cash at 8pm before you've checked.

Money: if the pump and injectors are fine, it's drain the tank, flush the lines, new filter, bleed it — usually R2 500 to R4 500. I can't promise you a total tonight, I haven't seen the bakkie. Tash's R40 000 is the worst case, not the only case.

My shop's in Umbilo, open Saturday 7 till 12. Thabo can drain it first thing if you get it to me.

**But borrow a bakkie for tomorrow anyway.** Don't plan your wedding around a drained tank — sort the cake and the sound system tonight and let the Isuzu wait.

You'll laugh at this one day. I put diesel in the boss's Golf in 1995, my first year as an apprentice — he still tells it at every braai. We also had a customer who did it twice in one year, same garage. We made him a sticker for the fuel flap.

Congrats on the wedding, bru. You're marrying her tomorrow either way. Just don't touch that key.
